title: ID0433626-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R0 170002804] truck cuts out at 56% battery capacity
description:

battery capacity.If there are 2 trucks (Volvo and eActros), the eActros only takes 70kW. On other public charging stations, there's no problem.
Solution: Customer changed something in EV -> waiting for customer's feedback

additional_info.subject: ID0433626-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R0 170002804] truck cuts out at 56% battery capacity CRM:02684000359
additional_info.body:
Hi José,
I managed to get a 56% session like the customer reported and here are the brief findings:
As you can see, we are in CurrentRequest<->CurrentResponse, which is the EnergyTransfer in V2G logs.
According to the standard, it's following correctly:
T10 - we can see from SCB logs the current reducing:
And then they send the PowerDeliveryRequest after the last CurrentRequest
With the Stop request.
This happens right after we do a algorithm change in the Converter allocation:
Here we are changing the MaxPwr from 220kW to 160kW due to the demands of the truck.
First of all we would like to understand if Mercedes is reacting to this change negatively and drops the session.
From the algorithm point of view there is no way to stop a session with this reallocation, there might be a incompatibility revolving around this power change.
Do you have any contact from Mercedes that you can show this information? If the answer from Mercedes is yes, then there is a fix in v8.X in which the algorithm is completely different in order to have these situations convered.
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: AW: W1T98340210828758 | WG: ID0433626-DC/Si-D/CH-[MP / R0 170002804] truck cuts out at 56% battery capacity CRM:02684000359
additional_info.body:
Hallo Sandro,
danke für die Informationen. Ich unterstütze gerne. Ein paar Punkte/Fragen die mir aufgefallen sind und wir prüfen sollten:
- Zumindest im unteren Auszug des Logs der letzten Ladesession sieht das zunächst nach einem normalen durch das Fahrzeug getriggerte Ladeende aus. Wäre es möglich uns das gesamte pcap file zukommen zu lassen? Uns würde der anfangs kommunizierte Target SoC interessieren. Da anscheinend jeweils bei 56% der Vorgang beendet wurde würde ich gerne ausschließen, dass nicht zufällig der Target SoC im Fahrzeug auf 56% gestellt ist.
@Bacher, Sandro (435)
Könntest du das zudem vom Kunden prüfen lassen?
Ein paar weitere Fragen:
Sind die Abbrüche reproduzierbar (auch bei anderem Soc)?
War im Fzg die Zündung eingeschaltet/ausgeschaltet?
Welcher Lademodus ist aktiv (Schnell, Eco, Reichweite)? Bei 56% SoC sind wir eigentlich noch ein gutes Stück entfernt, bevor es zu einer fahrzeugseitigen Reduktion in der Ladeleistung kommt.
- Zu folgendem Punkt
“
Here we are changing the MaxPwr from 220kW to 160kW due to the demands of the truck.
First of all we would like to understand if Mercedes is reacting to this change negatively and drops the session.”
Würde ich aktuell ausschließen. Beide Szenarien (Ladesäule verringert ihre MaxPwr weil wir weniger anfordern als auch Ladesäule verringert ihre MaxPwr weil sie nicht mehr leisten kann) waren bei unseren Tests bisher immer unauffällig.
Ladesäule verringert ihre MaxPwr weil sie nicht mehr leisten kann
Ladesäule verringert ihre MaxPwr weil wir weniger anfordern
Viele Grüße

additional_info.subject: Translation
additional_info.body:
Thank you for the information. I'm happy to help. Here are the points/questions that I noticed and that we should check:
At least in the lower excerpt of the last charging session log, this initially appears to be a normal vehicle-triggered end of charging. Would it be possible to send us the complete pcap file? We would be interested in the initially communicated Target SoC. Since the process apparently ended at 56% each time, I would like to rule out that the Target SoC in the vehicle isn't accidentally set to 56%. @Bacher, Sandro (435) Could you have this checked with the customer?
A few additional questions:
Are the interruptions reproducible (also at different SoC)?
Was the vehicle ignition switched on/off?
Which charging mode is active (Fast, Eco, Range)? At 56% SoC, we are still quite far from when vehicle-side reduction in charging power would occur.
Regarding this point:
"Here we are changing the MaxPwr from 220kW to 160kW due to the demands of the truck.
First of all, we would like to understand if Mercedes is reacting to this change negatively and drops the session."
I would currently rule this out. Both scenarios (charging station reduces its MaxPwr because we request less, as well as charging station reduces its MaxPwr because it cannot deliver more) have always been unremarkable in our tests so far.
Charging station reduces its MaxPwr because it cannot deliver more
Charging station reduces its MaxPwr because we request less
